environment.forecast_model: Ternary Bonsai 2 4B GGUF served by llama.cpp
environment.retrieval: Packaged Qwen and Kev results for matching inputs
environment.additional_chat: Separate Chromium sessions on the same five editable histories. The PDF and planning conversation used Nora.
environment.coverage: 30 initial cards, six completions, five website rankings and five longest-task questions. Additional sessions exercised PDF creation, editing, postponement and a follow-up planning question. This run used Linux, Chromium and GGUF. Native Windows, Bionic MLX and hosted Cohere were not exercised.

observations: For each stage, the dashboard budget and task count were compared with the saved cards. Each card includes the displayed estimate, saved minutes and range, model rationale, and comparison titles. Unchanged cards are omitted after the opening stage.

Website replies were checked against the summed off-task intervals in each history. Longest-task replies were checked against the greatest saved actual duration. A model-generated query originally grouped durations by category, so the planner now ranks individual tasks for those questions.

The numerical evidence and the model explanation can disagree. In Nora’s initial debugging forecast, Bonsai described a historical budget as 91 minutes. The original budget was 90 minutes and the recorded time was 137 minutes. On Ishan’s revised GPU task, the explanation predicted an overrun of the 75-minute budget, while the model supplied a 70-minute point estimate. Both are recorded in the walkthrough.

During an additional shared-server session the model process was killed. The dashboard surfaced fallback forecasts and kept accepting completions. The five isolated runs below show the result with each model endpoint running separately.

The chat send button was disabled while a PDF uploaded. Pressing Enter during that interval kept the draft. Sending once the upload finished submitted the task. The stored PDF was checked byte for byte after postponement.
